Event: `d47814b20c33a7ce0b29e4c3c87901fc` · 2026-09-24T15:42:09Z

> Verdict: OK with notes.
> 
> 1. (P2, kernel/src/mem.rs:1275) `budget_of(pid).ok_or(oom)?` in map_fixed uses OutOfMemory for a missing self-budget. Every other self-budget_of site in the kernel (handle.rs:214, endpoint.rs:158, process.rs:240, budget.rs:565/622, message.rs:697) uses Error::NotPermitted there, and model/src/kernel.rs uses Error::Dead (including its own map_fixed, kernel.rs:2438). Per libs/sys/src/error.rs's declared error set for map_fixed (`[InvalidArgument, OutOfMemory]`) and the fact pid is always the live caller, this branch is unreachable -- so it's not a live bug, but it's an unexplained third answer where the kernel has an established convention. Either match NotPermitted or `.expect("the running process has a budget")` to say it can't happen.
> 
> 2. (P2/note, kernel/src/mem.rs:1253-1302 vs process.rs:355-360) map_fixed's W+X/write-only flag check is a near-verbatim copy of process_map's -- both need it pre-validated because both use an unconditional `.expect()` afterward (unlike map_anon/map_run, which can let map_page_inner fail and roll back). A small shared helper, e.g. `fn check_map_flags(flags: MemoryFlags) -> Result<(), Error>`, used by both would remove the duplication without weakening either check. Not blocking -- 4 lines, well-commented reason it's needed twice.
> 
> Everything else checked as sound, non-duplicative:
> - `range_available_in`/`subtree_occupied` (arch/riscv/mem.rs) is a genuinely new whole-subtree-skip walk, not a per-page loop over `address_available_in`; correctly mirrored by the model's `range_free` (a single BTreeMap::range lookup, model/src/kernel.rs:1074-1081) -- both needed given addr/len are fully attacker-controlled.
> - The two-step OOM check (pages alone, then pages+tables) matches the model's map_fixed exactly and is justified (skips walking tables_needed for a request already too big to afford).
> - libs/sys and model/src/{gen,syscall,trace,mutation}.rs additions are boilerplate following each file's existing per-call pattern -- nothing unnecessary.
> - USER_BASE -> page-0-allowed change is applied consistently; no leftover references anywhere.
> 
> Merge verdict: OK with notes.
